soundness_flags.label: Definitions of M_n, G_n, N_n and L_G/L_N
soundness_flags.one_line: The branches are classes of law-and-fit triples but the risks take suprema over P in those classes and use E_P only, leaving the fitted-function randomness and the relevant projection from triples to evaluation laws undefined.

soundness_flags.label: Cubic ACE inversion and adaptive upper frontier
soundness_flags.one_line: The proposed score estimates only kappa_3 while fixing residual mean and variance at 0 and 1; with fitted residuals T-hat_g(X), the requisite estimated Appell score must also account for residual first and second cumulants, so the stated inversion denominator and B_n control are not defined by the construction.

soundness_flags.label: Detection-boundary and Pareto-lower-frontier statements
soundness_flags.one_line: The clauses 'up to the Gaussian logarithmic factor if unavoidable' and 'with any unavoidable factor reported' do not specify a theorem conclusion; state a d_n^- lower bound, a d_n lower bound under an added construction condition, or make removal of Lambda_n a separate OEQ.

soundness_flags.label: Definition of Lambda_n and Proposition 3
soundness_flags.one_line: Lambda_n=log(1/eps_g_n)/log n is undefined at eps_g_n=0, although the representative-regime proposition explicitly sets eps_g_n=0.

soundness_flags.label: Proposition 2: absolute-modulus symmetry
soundness_flags.one_line: Symmetry of the absolute cross-modulus follows immediately by swapping P and Q in its definition; retain only a precisely defined, nontrivial scalarization consequence if it is needed.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv v3, 7 November 2025; public version corresponding to NeurIPS 2025
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper proves a Gaussian SAE lower bound with its stated logarithmic factor, estimates residual cumulants under independent sub-Gaussian treatment noise, and gives ACE point-estimation bounds under a fixed positive cumulant lower bound; its estimated cubic polynomial uses cumulants through the required orders.
Theorem 5 gives the conditional-Gaussian obstruction to second-order orthogonal PLM moments; Theorems 8--10 construct/analyze non-Gaussian higher-order moments in their stated regimes.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Summary and Section 4, inference in partially linear models
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article presents cross-fitted Neyman-orthogonal DML and its partially linear-model inference application.
The paper obtains a CATE minimax lower bound using a localized fuzzy-hypotheses construction and supplies a matching local-polynomial estimator in a smooth CATE model.
The manuscript proposes perturb-and-filter DML confidence sets for slow nuisance learning; it does not claim treatment-cumulant adaptation.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace the cubic score by the full split-sample cumulant/Appell polynomial, including estimated residual first and second cumulants (or explicitly center and studentize residuals), then rederive the denominator and finite-sample interval radius.

Define the experiment and risks either conditional on fixed training-realized fits or jointly over training/evaluation data, and make L_G and L_N suprema over an explicitly projected law-and-fit class.
Split the logarithmic-loss issue into exact alternatives: prove the frontier at d_n^- now and make removal of Lambda_n a separately labelled fuzzy-Hermite OEQ with a concrete success criterion.
Delete the modulus-symmetry proposition or replace it with a formally defined scalarized minimax risk and a non-definitional comparison theorem.

recommended_next_step: Revise the inferential object and cubic-score construction before Stage 0; the shrinking-cumulant branchwise-frontier kernel remains novel and potentially flagship-grade.
